The record:
Write the overview of the executive synopsis for the incident on io-shop below: a short paragraph in plain words, for the people who lead the company rather than the engineers who responded - what happened, how long it lasted, what it cost the business and the people who responded, and how it was resolved.

What a reader saw: Shoppers saw nothing wrong, but the shop's metrics stopped being collected
Why, in plain words: A configuration change renamed the label the monitoring system uses to find the shop's figures, and the monitoring setup most likely still looked for the old name, so it stopped collecting them.

Figures:
- How long it lasted: 6m 45s {duration}
- What it cost the shop in takings (estimated by Argus): none {customer_loss}
- Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to this one.

What was done to end it:
- Argus: rolled back the deployment of io-shop - confirmed, still in place - automatic sync left off
- Argus: proposed a fix, PR #546 - opened as a draft

Name {duration} and {customer_loss} in your overview.
Write no figure yourself - not in digits, not spelled out, and not as a word that sizes it ("a brief outage", "a minor loss", "tripled"). Where a figure goes, write its name, braces and all, and the synopsis writes the figure in.
Say nothing about how the incident was resolved beyond what the list of what was done says: a draft fix has not run, and nothing it would do has happened.
Speak of Argus by name, never as "we", "our" or "us": Argus is the system that responded, and each line of what was done says who did it.
Where you say who was affected, say which ones, as the cause does, or that some were, where it does not say which - never how many, and never all of them, where the cause does not say all.
Keep "likely" on what the cause says is likely, and only there.

Call submit_executive_overview with your overview.

The postmortem it is written from:
Shoppers saw nothing wrong, but the shop's metrics stopped being collected
Incident: MetricsAbsent on io-shop
Date: Nov 11, 2026, 03:21 to 03:27:45 UTC, metrics missing until then
Status: Draft. 1 of 6 action items are done.
Written by: Argus Postmortem agent, Nov 11, 2026, 03:48:31 UTC. Not reviewed yet. Each part is as of when the work it reports ended, which the timeline dates; who ended the incident is as of now.
First told: Argus posted in Slack, Nov 11, 2026, 03:27:07 UTC
Ended by: Argus: rolled back the deployment of io-shop - confirmed, still in place

Summary
No metrics were collected from 03:21 UTC until they resumed at 03:27:45 UTC, 6 minutes 45 seconds later. The service's own logs reach into that stretch until 03:26 UTC, as far as they were read. The shop's takings fell short of the same hours on earlier weeks by no more than those hours vary on their own, if at all. A configuration change renamed the label the monitoring system uses to find the shop's figures, and the monitoring setup most likely still looked for the old name, so it stopped collecting them. What Argus did: rolled back the deployment of io-shop (can be put back) - confirmed, still in place. Argus opened a draft fix, PR #546, for a person to review and merge. Argus left automatic sync of io-shop off, to be turned back on once its repository says what should run (AI-3). Any deploy that names the metrics port differently from the name the scrape configuration looks for, whether the same rename going out again or one of the two files changing without the other, would quietly stop the shop's metrics being collected again without raising any error.

Impact
6m 45s - onset until the metrics resumed
not measured by the metrics - peak error rate
not counted by the metrics - requests failed
none - customer loss (estimated)
AL1: What the alert found: No metrics received from io-shop since 2026-11-11T03:21:00Z - 6m with no sample, against a scrape interval of 15 seconds. The series stopped rather than crossing a threshold, so nothing here says whether the shop is well: these minutes have no readings to judge, not readings that look bad.
The metrics stop at the onset, so the duration is how long they were missing, until they resumed - not a stretch the service is known to have spent broken.
The service's own logs reach into the stretch the metrics missed until 03:26 UTC: G46bc, Gbac1, Gad41. They were read up to then. As far as they show, the service went on serving as it had before the metrics stopped.

Root cause and contributing factors
The scrape configuration finds the shop's metrics target by the port's name, not its number, and the deploy renamed that port in deploy/values-production.yaml from metrics to http-metrics without changing the name deploy/scrape.yaml selects, which is still metrics. The selector then matched no port, and the scraper had nothing left to collect. It rests on F1, a reading of the source nothing ran, so it is unverified.
Causal chain
symptom No sign was seen that anyone using the shop had a problem. What was seen instead was that the shop's metrics stopped arriving, and no samples covered the minutes after they stopped.
  Evidence:
    AL1
    T4 03:27:29 Investigator Agent: Read the service's metrics - they stop after the minute at 03:20, and nothing covers the minutes since
    G46bc ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ClientDisconnected: the shopper closed the connection - before the metrics stopped: 9 occurrences in 7 minutes, 03:14–03:20. After they stopped: 9 occurrences in 5 minutes, 03:22–03:26
    Gbac1 WARN io-shop: account page error rate at #% over the last minute - before the metrics stopped: 6 occurrences in 7 minutes, 03:14–03:20; # was 0.50% to 1.50%, typically 0.50%, highest at 03:15. After they stopped: 5 occurrences in 5 minutes, 03:22–03:26; # was 0.50% to 1.50%, typically 1.00%, highest at 03:22
    Gad41 INFO io-shop: account pages rendered normally - before the metrics stopped: 1 occurrence in 1 minute, 03:18. After they stopped: 1 occurrence in 1 minute, 03:21
why 1 The deploy of revision 9f4ad14 at 03:21:22 UTC changed one value in deploy/values-production.yaml: it renamed the metrics port from metrics to http-metrics and left the port number at 9090. When read at 03:27:38 UTC, all 3 replicas were running that revision.
  Evidence:
    P2 03:21:22 UTC deploy 9f4ad14 by kuki: from the ohadraz/Argus-Demo-Target-App repository's deploy/ directory
    D1 Deployment of revision 9f4ad14 to io-shop, compared against e283ba3 - the revision deployed before it.
    T12 03:27:38 Investigator Agent: Read how far the deployment had rolled out - all 3 replicas run revision 9f4ad14, deployed at 03:21:22
  Ruled out:
    The earlier deploy of revision e283ba3 at Nov 10, 23:21:22 UTC. Metrics were collected with it in place up to the minute at 03:20 UTC. Once the rollback put that revision back, the metrics could be read again.
      T4
      M1 03:27:45 Rolled back the deployment of io-shop for C1: confirmed, still in place
      T19 03:28:04 Mitigation Agent: Looked at the service - its metrics could be read again from 03:27
    A flag change by anyone but Argus: Argus read the flag provider's history - 0 flag changes by anyone but Argus, the 1 hour before 03:27:39.
      T15
why 2 The scrape configuration picks the shop's metrics target by the port's name and was still looking for metrics, so after the rename it matched no port and had nothing to collect.
  Evidence:
    S1 deploy/values-production.yaml at 9f4ad14
    F1 What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed - nothing ran its test or its fix
Contributing factors
- No check was seen that would catch the port name in deploy/values-production.yaml no longer matching the name the scrape configuration selects. The values file's own comment says nothing in the shop reads that name, and that a name nothing matches fails silently. A rename in one file could therefore ship without the other file changing. (AI-4)
- The MetricsAbsent alert fired 3 minutes 33 seconds later than its evaluation interval, the scraping allowance and the minute-level dating of the stop can explain. The record does not show what took the extra time. (AI-5)

Hypotheses considered
 | Hypothesis | Confidence | Result
C1 | The deploy of 9f4ad14 at 03:21:22 UTC changed one value in deploy/values-production.yaml, metrics.portName from metrics to http-metrics. The metrics rows stop at 03:20 UTC. The shop kept serving normally: logs across the gap show only the usual low-rate ClientDisconnected errors. What broke is the reporting, not the service. | 0.55 | confirmed
C2 | The metrics port name was renamed from metrics to http-metrics on purpose in the 03:21:22 UTC deploy, and the scrape configuration still selects the old name. The scrape therefore finds no target and the series stops. | 0.35 | confirmed, as tested for C1

Trigger
deploy/values-production.yaml changed at 03:21:22 UTC, in the deploy of 9f4ad14 that kuki started.

Resolution
 | Time (UTC) | Action | By | Kind | Outcome
M1 | 03:27:45 | Rolled back the deployment of io-shop for C1 | Argus | can be put back | confirmed, still in place - automatic sync left off
 | 03:29:37 | Proposed a fix: PR #546 | Code-Fix Agent | nothing to put back | opened as a draft

Detection
The metrics on io-shop stopped at 03:21 UTC. MetricsAbsent fired at 03:27:03 UTC, 6 minutes 3 seconds later - its rule fires as soon as its condition holds.

Action items
Item | Action | Type | Owner | Tracking | Status
AI-1 | Rolled back the deployment of io-shop | mitigate | Argus | - | done
AI-2 | Review and merge the proposed fix | prevent | unassigned | PR #546 | open
AI-3 | Turn automatic sync of io-shop back on once its repository says what should run - until then nothing merged reaches it, and turned on sooner it puts back what the repository says, undoing what Argus changed by hand | mitigate | unassigned | - | open
AI-4 | Add a pre-deploy CI check, applied to every service and not only io-shop, that fails any change where a scrape endpoint's port name matches none of the port names the deployment renders. | prevent | unassigned | - | open
AI-5 | Find what delayed the MetricsAbsent alert on io-shop by 3 minutes 33 seconds beyond what its evaluation accounts for, and remove that delay. | detect | unassigned | - | open
AI-6 | Link MetricsAbsent on io-shop to the on-call rotation so that a person is paged when it fires. | process | unassigned | - | open

Lessons learned
What went well
- 35 seconds after the alert was raised, the Investigator Agent read what the deployment of 9f4ad14 changed.
- 42 seconds after the alert was raised, the Mitigation Agent rolled back the deployment of io-shop for C1.
- 1 minute 1 second after the alert was raised, the Mitigation Agent judged the action CONFIRMED.
- 2 minutes 34 seconds after the alert was raised, the Code-Fix Agent proposed a fix as a draft pull request - PR #546.
What went wrong
- The alert came 3 minutes 33 seconds later than the 2 minutes 30 seconds accounted for by its evaluation at intervals of 1 minute, an unmeasured allowance of 30 seconds for scraping and storing its samples and the whole minute the metrics' stopping is measured to. The record does not show what took the rest.
- When MetricsAbsent fired on io-shop, nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to it.
Where it got lucky
Nothing.

Response effort
none - engineer time
141,888 - tokens spent by Argus

Supporting information
The incident's walk: http://localhost:8000/incidents/615124fe-4de5-41aa-8568-b14db4c8202d
The fix it proposed: PR #546 (https://github.com/ohadraz/Argus-Demo-Target-App/pull/546) opened as a draft. The record holds nothing about it after that.
Changes to production read
P1 | Nov 10, 2026, 23:21:22 UTC deploy e283ba3 by kuki: from the ohadraz/Argus-Demo-Target-App repository's deploy/ directory
P2 | 03:21:22 UTC deploy 9f4ad14 by kuki: from the ohadraz/Argus-Demo-Target-App repository's deploy/ directory
Flags read, none came back.
Log messages read (UTC)
G46bc | ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ClientDisconnected: the shopper closed the connection - before the metrics stopped: 9 occurrences in 7 minutes, 03:14–03:20. After they stopped: 9 occurrences in 5 minutes, 03:22–03:26
Gbac1 | WARN io-shop: account page error rate at #% over the last minute - before the metrics stopped: 6 occurrences in 7 minutes, 03:14–03:20; # was 0.50% to 1.50%, typically 0.50%, highest at 03:15. After they stopped: 5 occurrences in 5 minutes, 03:22–03:26; # was 0.50% to 1.50%, typically 1.00%, highest at 03:22
Gad41 | INFO io-shop: account pages rendered normally - before the metrics stopped: 1 occurrence in 1 minute, 03:18. After they stopped: 1 occurrence in 1 minute, 03:21
What each deployment looked into changed
D1 | Deployment of revision 9f4ad14 to io-shop, compared against e283ba3 - the revision deployed before it.
modified deploy/values-production.yaml
  @@ -43,7 +43,7 @@ autoscaling:
   # the only sign is that the series stops.
   metrics:
     port: 9090
  -  portName: metrics
  +  portName: http-metrics
   
   # Where the rendered-summary cache lives.
   #
What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed - nothing ran its test or its fix
F1 | The fault: deploy/values-production.yaml sets metrics.portName: http-metrics (changed in 9f4ad14). deploy/scrape.yaml, the ServiceMonitor, still picks its scrape endpoint by the port name metrics. Its own comment says it picks by name, that the two names must match, and that nothing checks this: a name that matches no port gives an empty target list, not an error. So when the rename went out, the shop kept serving, but Prometheus had nothing left to scrape.

The fix: change endpoints[0].port in deploy/scrape.yaml to http-metrics, matching the value now in production. This keeps the deploy that renamed the port instead of reverting it. Rolling the values back to metrics without this change would just leave the same trap for the next rename.

The test: tests/io_shop/test_scrape_config.py reads both files from the repository root. It takes portName from the metrics: block of values-production.yaml and every port: under endpoints: in scrape.yaml, and asserts that each endpoint's port equals portName. It uses plain text parsing, so it adds no YAML library dependency. Against the files as they stood before this change, it is written to fail (metrics vs http-metrics). It turns the agreement the comment says nothing enforces into something CI checks, so the next rename that changes only one file fails a test instead of breaking the metrics silently.
What ran, read at the revision running when the alert fired
S1 | deploy/values-production.yaml at 9f4ad14
Assumptions
- Exchange rate: EUR converted at 0.92191 per USD, published 2026-11-10
- No engineer minutes: no on-call incident was linked to this one, so nobody was paged to respond

The document, by field:
overview: For {duration}, the io-shop online shop kept working normally for shoppers, but the monitoring system stopped collecting the shop's figures. A configuration change had renamed the label the monitoring system uses to find those figures, and the monitoring setup most likely still looked for the old name. Argus estimates the cost to the shop in takings at {customer_loss}. No on-call staff were paged, because no on-call incident was linked to this one. Argus ended the incident by rolling back the io-shop deployment. The rollback is confirmed and still in place, and automatic sync has been left off. Argus has also proposed a fix, but it is only a draft and has not been applied.

Not to be judged:
  - Names in braces, such as {duration}, are figures code writes in from the list of figures in the ask. They are not judged.
  - The overview is written in plain words for the people who lead the company. A claim said more plainly than the postmortem says it is grounded where it means the same.

Judge every claim in the document, and answer by calling judge_claims.

tools.description: Submit every claim in the document, each either as supported or as flagged. Supported: the document's own words, quoted exactly, and the record's rows that support it. Flagged: the document's own words, quoted exactly, why, and the record's rows that contradict it (none where no row speaks to it at all). Empty lists say the document makes no claim to judge.

why.description: One sentence: what the record holds instead. Never empty.
